title: Warm-up: 1 + 1 = 2
plain: A test problem for checking the submission pipeline. Prove that 1 + 1 = 2.
math: Prove $1+1=2$ in $\mathbb{N}$.

title: Lonely runner with one fast runner
plain: Runners have speeds 1, 2, 3 and some larger speed m. Work out exactly how lonely a stationary runner is guaranteed to get, depending on m.
math: Compute $\delta(m)=\sup_t\min(\|t\|,\|2t\|,\|3t\|,\|mt\|)$ in closed form for all integers $m\ge4$.

title: Infinite Prime Nim losses
plain: Prime Nim has infinitely many losing pile sizes (a known theorem, since primes have arbitrarily large gaps). Show they are rare.
math: Let $L=\{n: G(n)=0\}$ for the subtraction game with prime moves ($|L|=\infty$ is known). Prove $L$ has natural density $0$.

title: Lean golf is NP-hard
plain: Show that finding the shortest proof using only a few basic Lean tactics is computationally hard.
math: Prove NP-hardness of: given a Lean 4 goal and $k$ in unary, is there a proof using only intro, apply, exact, rfl with at most $k$ steps?

title: Graceful spider forests
plain: Spiders are trees with one central branching vertex. Show forests of spiders have the distinct-difference labeling.
math: For any forest of spiders with $m$ edges and $c$ components, find a bijection $V\to\{0,\dots,m+c-1\}$ with distinct edge differences.

title: Shuffle with a cut
plain: Do a perfect shuffle, then cut k cards from top to bottom, and repeat. How many repetitions bring the deck back?
math: For the permutation $c_k\circ\sigma_{\text{out}}$ on $2n$ cards, determine its order as a function of $n$ and $k$.

title: Delayed firefighters
plain: Fire spreads in four directions, but a firefighter assigned now only takes effect a turn later. How many per turn are needed?
math: On $\mathbb{Z}^2$ with 4-neighbour spread, cells chosen at turn $t$ become protected at turn $t+1$. Find the least per-turn number that contains a single fire.

title: Aperiodic polykite census
plain: The "hat" is made of 8 kites and tiles the plane only non-periodically. Find every such shape made of at most 12 kites.
math: Enumerate all polykites with $\le12$ kites (from the $\{6,3\}$ kite grid) that tile $\mathbb{R}^2$ but admit no periodic tiling.

title: Drum tones of superellipses
plain: Among regions x^p + y^p ≤ r of unit area, the circle (p = 2) has the lowest tone and the square (p = ∞) is back up high. Show the tone rises steadily as p goes from 2 to infinity.
math: Let $D_p=\{|x|^p+|y|^p\le r_p^p\}$ with $r_p$ chosen so $|D_p|=1$, and let $\lambda_1(p)$ be its first Dirichlet eigenvalue. Prove $\lambda_1$ is strictly increasing on $[2,\infty)$.

title: Voice leading is NP-hard
plain: Moving n voices through a chord progression with the least total motion while avoiding parallel fifths should be computationally hard.
math: Show NP-hardness of minimizing $\sum_t\sum_i |x_{t+1,i}-x_{t,i}|$ over voicings of a given chord sequence with $n$ voices, subject to no parallel perfect fifths.

title: Real-rank hyperoperations
plain: Addition, multiplication and exponentiation are ranks 1, 2, 3 of one ladder. Find natural rules that fix a unique operation at every real rank in between.
math: Find axioms (analytic in $s$, $a[s{+}1](b{+}1)=a[s](a[s{+}1]b)$, agreement with $+,\times,\uparrow$ at $s=1,2,3$) that determine $a[s]b$ uniquely for real $s\in[1,3]$, and prove uniqueness.

title: Adversarial 2048
plain: An opponent places every new tile in 2048 as unhelpfully as possible. What is the biggest tile you can still guarantee?
math: On the $4\times4$ board where an adversary chooses each spawn's position and value in $\{2,4\}$, determine the largest tile the player can force.

title: Blank jigsaw
plain: A jigsaw with no picture can only be solved from piece shapes. How few edge shapes force a unique solution?
math: Find the asymptotics in $n$ of the least number of edge types such that some $n\times n$ jigsaw has exactly one assembly (up to rotation of the whole).

title: Quarter-tone all-interval rows
plain: Count the tone rows in 24-note tuning that use every interval exactly once.
math: Count permutations of $\mathbb{Z}_{24}$ whose successive differences are all distinct nonzero residues, and find their growth rate for $\mathbb{Z}_{2m}$.

title: Small Keller maps in 3D
plain: The 2026 counterexamples to the Jacobian conjecture have fairly high degree. Is there one of degree 5 or less?
math: Decide whether some $F:\mathbb{C}^3\to\mathbb{C}^3$ with $\deg F\le5$ and $\det DF\in\mathbb{C}^\times$ has no polynomial inverse.

title: Penrose firefighter
plain: Fire spreads along a Penrose tiling's edges. How many firefighters per turn can trap any fire?
math: On the vertex graph of a Penrose rhomb tiling, find the least $k$ such that protecting $k$ vertices per turn contains a fire from any single vertex.

title: Three-pile shuffle group
plain: Using the six ways to stack three piles in a perfect shuffle, which rearrangements of the deck can you reach?
math: Determine the subgroup of $S_{3n}$ generated by the six 3-pile perfect shuffles (all pile orders), for every $n$.

title: Counting 16 × 16 Sudoku
plain: Count the essentially different 16 × 16 Sudoku grids, ignoring symmetries, to three significant figures.
math: Determine the automorphism group $\Gamma$ of the $16\times16$ Sudoku constraint structure and estimate $|\text{grids}/\Gamma|$ to 3 significant figures.

title: Hyperbolic firefighter budgets
plain: In a hyperbolic tiling, fire spreads exponentially, so no fixed crew stops it. How fast must the crew grow?
math: On the $\{7,3\}$ tiling graph, find the minimal growth of budgets $k_t$ (firefighters at turn $t$) that contains any single fire.

title: Packing seven-pointed stars
plain: Find the densest way to pack identical seven-pointed stars in the plane.
math: Determine the maximal packing density of congruent copies of the regular star polygon $\{7/2\}$.

title: Formalize 3D Kakeya
plain: Turn the 2025 proof of the three-dimensional Kakeya conjecture into a compact computer-checked proof.
math: Produce a Lean 4 formalization of the Wang–Zahl theorem ($\dim_H K=3$ for Kakeya $K\subset\mathbb{R}^3$) in under 50,000 lines beyond Mathlib.

title: Formalize the sofa
plain: Turn Baek's proof that Gerver's sofa is optimal into a computer-checked proof.
math: Formalize in Lean 4 the statement and proof that the moving sofa constant equals the area of Gerver's sofa.

title: Optimal origami base
plain: Folders design animal shapes by packing circles on paper. Find the smallest paper needed for every stick figure with six legs or fewer.
math: For every weighted tree with $\le6$ leaves, determine the minimum square side admitting a uniaxial base (optimal circle–river packing), with certificates.

title: Hamiltonian induced subgraphs of S_N
plain: Show deciding whether a given set of numbers can be lined up so neighbours sum to squares is NP-complete.
math: Prove NP-completeness of: given $A\subset\mathbb{N}$ (in binary), decide whether $S_\infty[A]$ has a Hamiltonian path.

title: Period-doubling torus bundles
plain: Build a once-punctured torus bundle by reading the period-doubling word as a product of the two basic shear matrices. Show its hyperbolic volume per letter settles to a limit as the word grows.
math: Let $W_n\in\{a,b\}^{2^n}$ be the length-$2^n$ prefix of the fixed point of $a\mapsto ab,\ b\mapsto aa$, let $\phi_n$ be $W_n$ with $a\mapsto R=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$, $b\mapsto L=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$, and let $M_n$ be the (hyperbolic) once-punctured torus bundle with monodromy $\phi_n$. Prove that $\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathrm{vol}(M_n)/2^n$ exists.

title: Chaos in the symmetric ABC flow
plain: The ABC flow with all three coefficients equal to 1 is a classical steady solution of the Euler equations on the 3-torus. Prove it is genuinely chaotic.
math: Prove that the flow of $\dot x=\sin z+\cos y,\ \dot y=\sin x+\cos z,\ \dot z=\sin y+\cos x$ on $\mathbb T^3$ has positive topological entropy.

title: Sup norms on the Fermat quartic
plain: On a sphere, some eigenfunctions pile up at the poles as much as possible. Show this cannot happen on the surface x⁴+y⁴+z⁴ = 1.
math: Let $S=\{x^4+y^4+z^4=1\}$ with the induced metric and $\Delta\varphi=-\lambda\varphi$, $\|\varphi\|_{L^2(S)}=1$. Prove that $\|\varphi\|_{L^\infty(S)}=o(\lambda^{1/4})$ as $\lambda\to\infty$.

title: Shifted Fujita equation
plain: In the plane, every positive solution of u_t = Δu + u² blows up. Does this survive when the square is replaced by the product of values one unit to the left and right?
math: Let $e=(1,0)$. Prove or disprove: every solution of $u_t=\Delta u+u(x-e,t)\,u(x+e,t)$ on $\mathbb R^2$ with $0\le u_0\in C_c(\mathbb R^2)$, $u_0\not\equiv0$, blows up in finite time.

title: Minimal-mass blow-up with reflection
plain: In the 2D Schrödinger equation where each point feels the density at its mirror point, blow-up needs at least the ground-state mass. Classify the solutions that blow up with exactly that mass.
math: For $i u_t+\Delta u+|u(-x,t)|^2u=0$ on $\mathbb R^2$ with $\|u_0\|_{L^2}=\|Q\|_{L^2}$ ($Q$ the cubic ground state), prove that every $H^1$ solution blowing up in finite time equals, up to phase and scaling, the pseudo-conformal transform of $Q$ centred at the origin.

title: Frozen vortices for Kuramoto on a cube
plain: Identical Kuramoto oscillators on the grid of a cube surface tend to synchronize. Show that for large grids a stable state that is not synchronized also exists.
math: Let $Q_n$ be the vertex–edge graph of the $n\times n$ subdivided cube surface and $\dot\theta_i=\sum_{j\sim i}\sin(\theta_j-\theta_i)$. Prove that for all large $n$ there is a linearly stable equilibrium that is not of the form $\theta_i\equiv c$.

title: Monotile assembly threshold
plain: With one tile shape, deciding whether a region can be tiled is easy in some cases; with many shapes it is hard. Find the smallest number of shapes where it becomes hard.
math: Find the least $t$ such that some fixed set of $t$ polygons makes "does this finite region admit an exact tiling?" NP-complete, and prove all sets of fewer polygons give polynomial-time problems.

title: Square-sum coloring
plain: Join numbers that add up to a perfect square. Does the number of colors needed stay bounded forever?
math: Decide whether $\sup_N \chi(S_N)<\infty$.

title: Hyperbolic square peg
plain: Every closed curve in the hyperbolic plane should pass through the corners of some hyperbolic square.
math: Prove every Jordan curve in $\mathbb{H}^2$ contains the four vertices of a regular hyperbolic quadrilateral.

title: FLT, compressed
plain: Fermat's Last Theorem has a huge computer formalization effort. Do it in far fewer lines.
math: Give a Lean 4 proof of $x^n+y^n=z^n\Rightarrow xyz=0$ for $n\ge3$ using at most $10^5$ lines beyond current Mathlib.

title: Prime pancakes
plain: Sort pancakes by flipping only a prime number at a time. Find the worst-case number of flips asymptotically.
math: With prefix reversals of prime length, determine $\lim_n d(n)/n$ for the worst-case sorting distance $d(n)$.

title: Seven-free three primes
plain: Every large odd number should be a sum of three primes that never use the digit 7.
math: Prove every sufficiently large odd $N$ is $p_1+p_2+p_3$ with each $p_i$ prime and free of the decimal digit 7.

title: Blokus Duo
plain: Who wins two-player Blokus with perfect play?
math: Weakly solve Blokus Duo on the $14\times14$ board with standard starting points.

title: Square-sum cliques
plain: How many numbers can pairwise add up to perfect squares? Decide if there is a limit.
math: Decide whether $\omega(S_N)$ is bounded, i.e., whether there exist arbitrarily large sets of distinct positive integers with all pairwise sums square.

title: Distant-force blow-up
plain: The 2026 Navier–Stokes blow-up pushed fluid right where it broke. Make it break with a push kept far away.
math: Construct smooth compactly supported $f$ with $\operatorname{supp} f\cap B(x_*,1)=\emptyset$ such that 3D Navier–Stokes from rest blows up at $x_*$ in finite time.

title: Closed-form Euler blow-up
plain: Give smooth starting data for frictionless 3D fluid, written as an explicit formula, that blows up.
math: Find closed-form smooth finite-energy $u_0$ on $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose unforced Euler solution blows up in finite time.

title: Two fires
plain: Two fires start a distance d apart. How many firefighters per turn are needed, depending on d?
math: On $\mathbb{Z}^2$ with 4-neighbour spread, find the least $k(d)$ containing fires started at $(0,0)$ and $(d,0)$.

title: Building a firebreak
plain: Firefighters must build one connected wall, one cell per turn, each next to the last. Can they ever enclose the fire?
math: On $\mathbb{Z}^2$, each turn add one protected cell 8-adjacent to the previous one. Decide whether a single fire can be enclosed, and for which build rates.

title: Go on a torus
plain: Go on a 7 × 7 board that wraps around. What komi makes the game fair?
math: Determine the perfect-play score of Go on $\mathbb{Z}_7^2$ (area scoring, positional superko).

title: Worst-case Battleship
plain: What is the fewest shots that always sinks the standard fleet on a 10 × 10 board?
math: Compute the minimax number of shots to sink ships of lengths 5,4,3,3,2 on $10\times10$ against an adversary who may move ships consistently with past answers.

title: Random graceful forests
plain: Almost every random forest has the distinct-edge-difference labeling.
math: For a uniform random forest with $m$ edges and $c\sim\alpha m$ components, prove the graceful-forest labeling exists with probability $\to1$.

title: Random lonely runners
plain: With random speeds, runners get noticeably lonelier than the conjecture promises.
math: For i.i.d. uniform speeds in $[1,N]$, $N\gg n^3$, prove the loneliness gap exceeds $\frac1{n+1}+c\frac{\log n}{n^2}$ with probability $\to1$.

title: Sudoku resolution bounds
plain: Proving a large broken Sudoku has no solution should require long logical proofs.
math: Prove resolution refutations of unsatisfiable $n^2\times n^2$ Sudoku instances require size $2^{n^{\Omega(1)}}$ for some explicit family.

title: Prime-frequency synchrony
plain: Oscillators with frequencies set by logarithms of primes eventually synchronize when coupled strongly enough. Find the threshold.
math: For the Kuramoto model with $\omega_i=\log p_i$, prove a sharp synchronization threshold $K_c(N)$ and its asymptotics.

title: BB(5), compressed
plain: The Busy Beaver value BB(5) was proved with a large computer proof. Make it small.
math: Prove $BB(5)=47{,}176{,}870$ in Lean 4 in under 10,000 lines.

title: Four colors, compressed
plain: Make the computer-checked four color theorem much shorter.
math: Give a Lean 4 proof of the four color theorem in under 20,000 lines beyond Mathlib.

title: Emirps, almost
plain: Show infinitely many primes have a reversal with at most three prime factors.
math: Prove $\#\{p\le x: \Omega(\operatorname{rev}(p))\le3\}\to\infty$.

title: Shuffle-sorting
plain: Using any of the six 3-pile perfect shuffles each time, how many shuffles reach any reachable arrangement in the worst case?
math: Determine the diameter of the Cayley graph of the 3-pile shuffle group on $3n$ cards, asymptotically in $n$.

title: A four-dimensional einstein
plain: Find one 4D shape that fills 4D space but only without repeating.
math: Find a connected tile $T\subset\mathbb{R}^4$ that tiles $\mathbb{R}^4$ by isometries but admits no periodic tiling.

title: Firefighters on the front line
plain: Firefighters may only protect cells touching the fire. How many per turn are needed now?
math: On $\mathbb{Z}^2$ with protected cells required to be 4-adjacent to the burned set, find the least per-turn number containing a single fire.

title: Sudoku transversals
plain: In every completed big Sudoku, find a set of cells with one in each row, each column and each symbol.
math: Prove every $n^2\times n^2$ Sudoku grid, viewed as a Latin square, has a transversal.

title: Effective Riemann constants
plain: Extract explicit, usable prime-counting error bounds from the 2026 Riemann proof.
math: From the 2026 Lean proof, extract and formally verify $|\pi(x)-\operatorname{li}(x)|\le\frac{1}{8\pi}\sqrt{x}\log x$ for all $x\ge2657$.

title: Random Wang tiles
plain: Pick n random tile types with colored edges. How likely are they to tile the plane?
math: For $n$ Wang tiles with edge colours i.i.d. uniform in $[c]$, find the asymptotics of $\Pr(\text{tiles }\mathbb{Z}^2)$ as $n\to\infty$.

title: Random polykites
plain: Show almost no shapes made of many kites can tile the plane.
math: Prove the fraction of $k$-kite polykites that tile $\mathbb{R}^2$ decays exponentially in $k$.

title: Petersen Ramsey multiplicity
plain: In any two-coloring of a huge complete graph, how many single-color copies of the Petersen graph must appear, at least?
math: Determine the Ramsey multiplicity constant $\lim_n \min_{\text{2-col}} \#\text{mono } P / \#P \text{ in } K_n$ for the Petersen graph $P$.

title: Fire whirls
plain: Show the equations of buoyant flow allow a rotating column of fire that travels steadily.
math: Prove existence of a smooth traveling swirling solution of the 3D Boussinesq equations with a localized heat source.

title: Prime Golomb rulers
plain: Find the shortest ruler with marks only at prime positions where all distances between marks are different.
math: For each $n$, determine the minimal $L$ such that some set of $n$ primes in an interval of length $L$ has all pairwise differences distinct; find its asymptotics.

title: Three large consecutive factors
plain: Show infinitely many n have n, n + 1 and n + 2 each with a prime factor bigger than n^0.9.
math: Prove infinitely many $n$ with $\min\{P(n),P(n+1),P(n+2)\}>n^{0.9}$.

title: Hexagonal Lebesgue covering
plain: Find the smallest convex shape that can cover every set of diameter 1, if covering is by translation only, not rotation.
math: Determine $\min\{\mathrm{area}(K):K$ convex, every set of diameter $1$ has a translate inside $K\}$, and prove the minimiser is unique.

title: Square subtraction with prime piles
plain: In the game where you subtract a square, show infinitely many prime pile sizes are losing positions.
math: Prove infinitely many primes are P-positions of the subtract-a-square game.

title: Outer billiards around a superellipse
plain: Outer billiards around a smooth convex shape with positive curvature has only bounded orbits. Decide whether this survives for x⁴+y⁴ ≤ 1, whose curvature vanishes at four points.
math: Let $K=\{x^4+y^4\le1\}$ and let $T:\mathbb R^2\setminus K\to\mathbb R^2\setminus K$ be the outer billiard map ($T(p)$ is the reflection of $p$ in the point where the right-hand tangent line from $p$ touches $\partial K$). Decide whether every $T$-orbit is bounded.

title: Rupert superballs
plain: The cube can pass through a hole drilled in a copy of itself; the round ball cannot. Show every superball between them, |x|^p+|y|^p+|z|^p ≤ 1 with p > 2, can.
math: Let $B_p=\{|x|^p+|y|^p+|z|^p\le1\}$. Prove that for every $p\in(2,\infty)$ there are orthogonal projections $\pi_1,\pi_2$ onto planes and a rigid motion $\rho$ of the plane with $\rho(\pi_1(B_p))\subset\operatorname{int}\pi_2(B_p)$.

title: Charge on a Fermat conductor
plain: Put a unit of electric charge on a perfectly conducting body x⁴+y⁴+z⁴ ≤ 1. Show the surface charge is thinnest at the six flat points and thickest at the eight diagonal points.
math: Let $\mu$ be the Newtonian equilibrium measure of $K=\{x^4+y^4+z^4\le1\}$, with density $\rho$ with respect to surface area on $\partial K$. Prove that $\rho$ attains its minimum exactly at $(\pm1,0,0),(0,\pm1,0),(0,0,\pm1)$ and its maximum exactly at $3^{-1/4}(\pm1,\pm1,\pm1)$.

title: Strauss exponent for an oscillating source
plain: The wave equation with source |u|^p in 3D has small-data global existence exactly above the Strauss exponent 1+√2. Find the threshold when the source is multiplied by cos t.
math: For $u_{tt}-\Delta u=\cos(t)\,|u|^p$ on $\mathbb R^{1+3}$ with data $\varepsilon(f,g)$, $f,g\in C_c^\infty$, determine $p_c$ such that for $p>p_c$ solutions are global for all small $\varepsilon$, and for $1<p<p_c$ some data blow up for all small $\varepsilon$; decide whether $p_c=1+\sqrt2$.

title: Heat with a cosine reaction
plain: In u_t = u_xx + cos(x)u², the reaction averages to zero, but a second-order effect looks like +u³, the borderline Fujita case. Does every positive start blow up?
math: Prove or disprove: for every $0\le u_0\in C_c(\mathbb R)$, $u_0\not\equiv0$, the solution of $u_t=u_{xx}+\cos(x)\,u^2$ on $\mathbb R$ blows up in finite time.

title: Burgers with degenerate critical dissipation
plain: Critical half-Laplacian dissipation keeps Burgers smooth. Let that dissipation switch off at one point of the circle. Do shocks form there?
math: Let $a(x)=1-\cos x$ and consider $u_t+uu_x+\Lambda^{1/2}\big(a\,\Lambda^{1/2}u\big)=0$ on $\mathbb T$, $\Lambda=(-\partial_x^2)^{1/2}$. Decide whether every $u_0\in C^\infty(\mathbb T)$ yields a global smooth solution.

title: Permanent–Ampère equation
plain: Monge–Ampère sets the Hessian determinant to 1, and Jörgens showed its entire convex solutions are quadratics. Swap the determinant for the permanent.
math: Let $u\in C^4(\mathbb R^2)$ satisfy $u_{xx}u_{yy}+u_{xy}^2=1$, $u_{xx}>0$, $2u_{xy}^2<1$ everywhere (ellipticity). Prove or disprove that $u$ is a quadratic polynomial.

title: Critical NLS mass on the cube
plain: Focusing cubic Schrödinger blow-up in 2D needs the ground-state mass. On a cube surface the corners should lower the threshold to three quarters of it.
math: On the flat unit-cube surface $S$, consider $iu_t+\Delta u+|u|^2u=0$. Prove: $H^1$ data with $\|u_0\|_2^2<\tfrac34\|Q\|_{L^2(\mathbb R^2)}^2$ give global solutions, and for every $m>\tfrac34\|Q\|_2^2$ there is $H^1$ data of mass $m$ blowing up in finite time.

title: Lane–Emden with a shift
plain: Replace u² in the five-dimensional Lane–Emden equation by the square of u at a shifted point. Are there still no positive solutions?
math: Let $e\in\mathbb R^5$, $e\ne0$. Decide whether there is a positive $u\in C^2(\mathbb R^5)$ with $-\Delta u(x)=u(x+e)^2$ for all $x$.

title: Thue–Morse quantum walk
plain: A quantum walker on the line uses a Hadamard coin or a rotation coin according to the Thue–Morse sequence. Decide whether it spreads at full ballistic speed.
math: On $\ell^2(\mathbb Z)\otimes\mathbb C^2$ let $U=S\,C$, where $S$ shifts the up and down components by $+1$ and $-1$, and $C_n=H$ if $t_{|n|}=0$, $C_n=\begin{pmatrix}\cos\frac\pi3&\sin\frac\pi3\\-\sin\frac\pi3&\cos\frac\pi3\end{pmatrix}$ if $t_{|n|}=1$. For $\psi_0=\delta_0\otimes e_1$ decide whether $\limsup_{T\to\infty}\frac{\log\sum_n|n|^2\|(U^T\psi_0)(n)\|^2}{2\log T}=1$.

title: Four vortices on a square torus
plain: Three point vortices on a flat torus are integrable. Show four identical ones are not.
math: Let $H=-\sum_{i<j}G(z_i-z_j)$, with $G$ the Green function of $\mathbb C/(\mathbb Z+i\mathbb Z)$, for four unit vortices. Prove that after reduction by the translation symmetry the system has no real-analytic first integral independent of $H$.

title: Hadwiger's true constant
plain: If graphs needing many colors need not contain a full complete-graph minor, find how large a complete minor they must contain.
math: Find $c^*=\liminf_{t}\min\{h(G)/t:\chi(G)\ge t\}$, where $h$ is the Hadwiger number.

title: Icosahedral monotile
plain: Find a single 3D tile that fills space and forces five-fold, icosahedral symmetry in every tiling.
math: Find $T\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ tiling space such that every tiling by $T$ has icosahedral symmetry in its hull, or prove none exists.

title: Minimal four-color proof
plain: The four color theorem's proof checks a big list of map configurations. Find the smallest list that works.
math: Determine the minimum size of an unavoidable set of reducible configurations for planar triangulations, with proof of minimality.

title: Readable Riemann
plain: The 2026 Riemann proof is a giant machine-checked archive. Write a proof people can read.
math: Give a proof of the Riemann hypothesis of at most 100 pages acceptable to expert referees.

title: Short Riemann
plain: Shrink the 2026 machine-checked Riemann proof drastically.
math: Give a Lean 4 proof of `RiemannHypothesis` in at most 10,000 lines beyond Mathlib.

title: Small Hadwiger counterexample
plain: The claimed counterexamples to Hadwiger's conjecture are astronomically large. Find one under a million vertices.
math: Find $G$ with $|V(G)|<10^6$ and $h(G)<\chi(G)$, or prove every counterexample is larger.

title: Explicit Navier–Stokes blow-up
plain: Write down a forced Navier–Stokes blow-up as an explicit formula instead of a computer-assisted construction.
math: Give closed-form smooth $u_0,f$ on $\mathbb{R}^3$ for which the Navier–Stokes solution blows up in finite time.

title: Two of four
plain: Show infinitely many primes p have at least one more prime among p + 2, 2p + 1, 2p + 3.
math: Prove infinitely many primes $p$ have at least one of $p+2,\,2p+1,\,2p+3$ prime.

title: Unbounded Prime Nim
plain: Do the Prime Nim values grow without limit?
math: Decide whether $\sup_n G(n)=\infty$ for the prime subtraction game.

title: Kakeya discs
plain: What is the least volume needed to turn a flat disc to every orientation?
math: Determine $\inf$ volume of sets in $\mathbb{R}^3$ containing a unit disc in every orientation (positive by Marstrand), with an extremizer.

title: 3-SAT at density 4
plain: Give a fast algorithm that solves almost all random 3-SAT puzzles up to clause density 4.
math: Give a polynomial-time algorithm finding satisfying assignments of random 3-SAT with density $4.0$ with probability $1-o(1)$.

title: Prime ladders
plain: Change one digit at a time, staying prime. Show any two k-digit primes are linked by at most k + 1 steps.
math: In the graph on $k$-digit primes joined when differing in one decimal digit, prove $\operatorname{diam}\le k+1$ for all $k$.

title: Ringel for forests
plain: Split a complete graph on 2m + 1 vertices into identical copies of any given forest with m edges.
math: Prove $K_{2m+1}$ decomposes into $2m+1$ copies of any forest with $m$ edges.

title: Geodesic squares on surfaces
plain: Every smooth closed curve on a convex surface should pass through the corners of a square made of shortest paths.
math: Prove every smooth simple closed curve on a smooth convex surface inscribes a geodesic quadrilateral with equal sides and equal diagonals.

title: Hat spectrum is a Cantor set
plain: Show the energy levels of a particle hopping on a hat tiling form a dust of measure zero.
math: Prove the spectrum of the adjacency operator on the hat graph is a Cantor set of Lebesgue measure zero.

title: Smallest force for blow-up
plain: How weak can the push be and still make viscous fluid blow up?
math: Find the optimal exponent $a$ with $\inf\{\|f\|_{L^\infty}: \text{NS from rest blows up}\}\asymp \nu^{a}$.

title: Forced SQG blow-up
plain: Copy the 2026 forced Navier–Stokes blow-up for the surface quasi-geostrophic equation.
math: Construct smooth compactly supported $f$ such that forced SQG on $\mathbb{R}^2$ from rest blows up in finite time.

title: Integer-bijective Keller map
plain: Find a polynomial map with Jacobian 1 that shuffles integer points perfectly but has no polynomial inverse.
math: Find $F\in\mathbb{Z}[x]^n$, $\det DF\equiv1$, inducing a bijection of $\mathbb{Z}^n$ but not a polynomial automorphism.

title: Firebreak with wind
plain: How long must a firebreak be to save a round town from a wind-driven fire?
math: For front speed $a+b\cos\theta$ and a disc town at distance $D$, find the minimal length of a curve built at speed $\sigma$ that protects the town.

title: Twin-free stretches
plain: Find long stretches full of primes but containing no twin primes.
math: Prove there are intervals $[x,x+(\log x)^{1.1}]$ with $\ge(\log x)^{0.05}$ primes but no twin pair, for infinitely many $x$.

title: Big factors of p² + p + 1
plain: For primes p, show p² + p + 1 often has a very large prime factor.
math: Prove $P(p^2+p+1)>p^{1.5}$ for infinitely many primes $p$.

title: Lonely runner, bounded speeds
plain: Prove the lonely runner conjecture whenever all speeds are at most 10 times the number of runners.
math: Prove $\sup_t\min_i\|tv_i\|\ge\frac1{n+1}$ for all distinct $v_i\le10n$.

title: Lonely runners in 3D
plain: Runners move in three dimensions on a cube that wraps around. Find the guaranteed loneliness.
math: For $n$ pairwise independent $v_i\in\mathbb{Z}^3$, find the optimal $\delta_n$ with $\sup_t\min_i\|tv_i\|_{\mathbb{T}^3,\infty}\ge\delta_n$.

title: Keller maps of degree 4
plain: Show that every 3D polynomial map of degree at most 4 with constant Jacobian has a polynomial inverse.
math: Prove $F:\mathbb{C}^3\to\mathbb{C}^3$, $\deg F\le4$, $\det DF\in\mathbb{C}^\times$ implies $F$ is an automorphism.

title: Sofa stability
plain: Show that any sofa nearly as big as Gerver's must look nearly like Gerver's.
math: Prove a quantitative stability bound: $A(S)\ge A_G-\varepsilon$ implies $d_H(S,G)\le C\varepsilon^{\alpha}$ up to rigid motion.

title: Sudoku symmetry breaking
plain: Show that most big Sudoku grids have no symmetry at all.
math: Prove the proportion of $n^2\times n^2$ Sudoku grids with nontrivial automorphism tends to 0.

title: Lorenz attractor dimension
plain: Pin down the fractal dimension of the classic Lorenz attractor to two decimals, rigorously.
math: For $\sigma=10,\beta=8/3,\rho=28$, prove $2.06\le\dim_H\mathcal{A}\le2.07$.

title: Unit-distance barrier
plain: Show the 2026 number-field method for many equal distances can never reach exponent 1.1.
math: Prove every construction of the Alon–Bloom–Gowers–…–Sawin type (lattices from number fields of bounded class-field degree) gives $u(n)\le n^{1.1}$.

title: Three-pile shuffle cutoff
plain: Random three-pile shuffles mix a deck suddenly, after a precise number of shuffles. Find it.
math: For random compositions of uniformly chosen 3-pile shuffles on $3n$ cards, prove total-variation cutoff at $c\log n$ and find $c$.

title: Greedy independent sets in square sums
plain: Pick random numbers up to N one by one, skipping any that sum to a square with something already picked. How many do you end with?
math: Determine the asymptotic size of the random greedy independent set in $S_N$, in probability.

title: Gerver sofa contact points
plain: Prove Gerver's sofa touches the corridor walls in exactly the pattern Gerver described at every moment of its optimal motion, and that the motion is unique.
math: Prove the optimal motion of Gerver's sofa through the unit corridor is unique up to time reparametrization.

title: Spectre quantum walk spreading
plain: A quantum particle hopping on the spectre tiling should spread at a rate strictly between localization and free motion. Compute the exponent.
math: For $H$ the adjacency operator of a spectre tiling and $\psi_0=\delta_o$, prove $\langle|X|^2\rangle_T\asymp T^{2\beta}$ and determine $\beta$.

title: Hats in a torus
plain: Hats tile the plane only non-periodically, so they cannot tile a flat torus. Find the smallest uncovered fraction for packing hats on a flat torus of area A.
math: Let $g(A)$ be the least uncovered area over packings of congruent hats in flat tori of area $A$. Prove $g(A)\to\infty$ and determine its growth order in $A$.

title: Counting square-sum chains
plain: Count the ways to line up 1 to N with neighbours summing to squares. Find the leading growth.
math: Let $h(N)$ be the number of Hamiltonian paths of $S_N$. Prove $\log h(N)=(\tfrac12+o(1))N\log N$.

title: Discrete sofa
plain: Slide and rotate a polyomino by unit steps and quarter turns around the corner of a corridor k cells wide. Find the largest area possible, asymptotically.
math: Let $D(k)$ be the maximal number of cells of a polyomino that can pass the width-$k$ L-shaped corridor of $\mathbb{Z}^2$ by unit translations and $90^\circ$ rotations about lattice points (staying inside at all times). Prove $D(k)\sim ck^2$ and find $c$.

title: Square-plus-one collisions
plain: Count pairs n ≠ m up to x for which n² + 1 and m² + 1 have the same largest prime factor.
math: Find the asymptotic number of pairs $n<m\le x$ with $P(n^2+1)=P(m^2+1)$.

title: Codes avoiding square distances
plain: Find the largest set of binary strings of length n in which no two differ in a perfect-square number of positions. Find the exponential rate.
math: Let $A(n)$ be the largest $C\subseteq\{0,1\}^n$ with $d_H(x,y)$ never a positive perfect square for $x\ne y\in C$. Determine $\lim_n\frac1n\log_2A(n)$.

title: Primes with equal binary and ternary digit sums
plain: Show infinitely many primes have the same digit sum in base 2 as in base 3.
math: Prove infinitely many primes $p$ with $s_2(p)=s_3(p)$.

title: Smooth p²+1
plain: Show infinitely many primes p have p² + 1 built only from primes below √p.
math: Prove infinitely many primes $p$ with $P(p^2+1)<p^{1/2}$.

title: Turán density of a twisted triple system
plain: Find the largest density of a 3-uniform hypergraph that avoids a specific six-vertex configuration of six triples.

title: Partizan Prime Nim
plain: Left may remove a prime that is 1 mod 4, Right a prime that is 3 mod 4, from one pile. Describe the game values.
math: For the partizan subtraction game with $L=\{p\equiv1\ (4)\}$, $R=\{p\equiv3\ (4)\}$, prove every position is equal to a number or a number plus a switch of bounded temperature, and find the bound.

title: Prime-sum graph is Hamiltonian-connected
plain: Show you can line up 1 to 2n with neighbours summing to primes, starting with any odd number and ending with any even one.
math: Prove for all large $n$ and all odd $a$, even $b$ in $[2n]$, the prime-sum graph on $[2n]$ has a Hamiltonian $a$–$b$ path.

title: Rotation-proof lattice-point-poor shapes
plain: Find the shape in the plane with given area that contains the fewest integer lattice points after any rotation, asymptotically.
math: Determine the convex $K$ of area $A$ minimising $\sup_{\theta}\#(\rho_\theta K\cap\mathbb{Z}^2)$, asymptotically as $A\to\infty$, to second-order term.

title: Moser's worm in the sphere
plain: Find the smallest area region on the unit sphere that can cover every curve of length 1 after a rotation.
math: Determine $\inf\{\sigma(K):K\subset S^2$ covers every rectifiable curve of length $1$ up to $SO(3)\}$ to within $1\%$, and prove the infimum is attained by a set bounded by finitely many circular arcs or show it is not.

title: Ising with prime couplings
plain: On the integer line, couple spins i and j with strength 1 if i − j is prime. Decide whether there is a phase transition.
math: For the 1D Ising model with $J_{ij}=\mathbf 1[|i-j|\in\mathbb{P}]\,|i-j|^{-2}$, prove a phase transition at finite $\beta_c$ and determine whether the magnetization jumps.

title: Random digit deletion
plain: Repeatedly delete a random decimal digit of a number until it is prime or has one digit. Find the probability of ending at a prime from a typical large start.
math: For uniform $n\le x$ and random single-digit deletions, prove $\Pr(\text{the process meets a prime})\to c$ and determine whether $c<1$.

title: Formal verification depth of RH
plain: The Riemann hypothesis now has a Lean proof. Show it cannot be proved in a weak arithmetic like I-Sigma-1 plus exponentiation, or show it can.
math: Decide whether RH (as a $\Pi^0_1$ sentence) is provable in $\mathrm{I}\Sigma_1$, or in $\mathrm{EFA}$.

title: Permanent of the prime-sum matrix
plain: Find the asymptotic count of perfect matchings between odd and even numbers up to 2n whose sums are all prime.
math: Determine $\log\mathrm{per}(M_n)$ to $o(n)$ where $M_n=(\mathbf 1[2i-1+2j\text{ prime}])_{i,j\le n}$.

title: Unbounded excursions in prime maps
plain: For n ↦ P(n) + P(n+1), show some orbits climb above their starting value by any factor you like.
math: Prove $\sup_n\max_k f^k(n)/n=\infty$ for $f(n)=P(n)+P(n+1)$.

title: Prime Markov triples
plain: Show only finitely many Markov triples consist of three primes, or infinitely many.
math: Decide whether infinitely many solutions of $x^2+y^2+z^2=3xyz$ have $x,y,z$ all prime.

title: Thue–Morse Lorenz knots
plain: Turn the first 2^n letters of the Thue–Morse word into a periodic orbit of the Lorenz template. Show these knots are eventually hyperbolic and their volume grows proportionally to the word length.
math: Let $K_n$ be the Lorenz knot whose Lorenz word is the length-$2^n$ Thue–Morse prefix $t_0\cdots t_{2^n-1}$ with $0\mapsto x$, $1\mapsto y$ (this word is primitive). Prove that $S^3\setminus K_n$ is hyperbolic for all sufficiently large $n$ and that $\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathrm{vol}(S^3\setminus K_n)/2^n$ exists and is positive.

title: Knotted billiards in a regular tetrahedron
plain: A billiard ball bouncing periodically inside a regular tetrahedron traces a closed polygon. Show that infinitely many different knot types arise this way.
math: Call a periodic billiard trajectory in a regular tetrahedron $T\subset\mathbb R^3$ admissible if it avoids edges and vertices and is an embedded closed polygon. Prove that the set of knot types of admissible periodic trajectories is infinite.

title: Integrability of the egg-crate torus
plain: Take the surface z = ε sin x sin y over a flat square torus. Show its geodesic flow is never integrable, however small the bumps are.
math: For $\varepsilon>0$ let $g_\varepsilon$ be the metric on $\mathbb R^2/(2\pi\mathbb Z)^2$ induced by the graph $z=\varepsilon\sin x\sin y$ in $\mathbb R^3$. Prove that for every $\varepsilon>0$ the geodesic flow of $g_\varepsilon$ has no real-analytic first integral on $T^*\mathbb T^2\setminus 0$ that is functionally independent of the Hamiltonian.

title: Simple closed geodesics on the Fermat quartic
plain: On the surface x⁴+y⁴+z⁴ = 1 the nine symmetry planes cut out nine simple closed geodesics. Are there only finitely many simple closed geodesics altogether?
math: Let $S=\{x^4+y^4+z^4=1\}$ with the metric induced from $\mathbb R^3$. The planes $x=0,y=0,z=0,x=\pm y,y=\pm z,x=\pm z$ meet $S$ in simple closed geodesics. Decide whether $S$ has finitely many simple closed geodesics (as unparametrized curves), and if so whether these nine are all of them.

title: How nearly can tetrahedra close up
plain: A chain of regular tetrahedra glued face to face can never close exactly. Find the exact exponential rate at which the best near-closure improves with chain length.
math: For a regular tetrahedron $T_0$, a chain of length $n$ is $T_0,\dots,T_n$ with $T_{k+1}$ the reflection of $T_k$ in a face not shared with $T_{k-1}$. Let $g(n)$ be the minimum over chains of the Hausdorff distance between $T_n$ and $T_0$ (always positive). Prove that $\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac1n\log g(n)=-\frac{\log 3}{6}$.

title: Capacities of the 4D superball
plain: Viterbo's conjecture that all symplectic capacities agree on convex bodies is false in general. Do they agree on the 4D ball x⁴+y⁴+z⁴+w⁴ ≤ 1?
math: Let $U=\{x_1^4+y_1^4+x_2^4+y_2^4\le1\}\subset(\mathbb R^4,\omega_0)$. Decide whether the Gromov width of $U$ equals its Ekeland–Hofer–Zehnder capacity (the minimal action of a closed characteristic on $\partial U$).

title: Free-boundary disks in a superball
plain: In a round ball the only free-boundary minimal disks are flat. In the superball x⁴+y⁴+z⁴ ≤ 1, is there one that is not a flat slice?
math: Let $B=\{x^4+y^4+z^4\le1\}$. Decide whether there is an embedded minimal disk $\Sigma\subset B$ with $\partial\Sigma\subset\partial B$ meeting $\partial B$ orthogonally that is not contained in a plane.

title: Riesz-transform Schrödinger equation
plain: Couple a 2D Schrödinger wave to the Riesz transform of its own density. Mass is conserved but there is no energy. Do smooth solutions live forever?
math: Consider $i u_t+\Delta u=u\,R_1(|u|^2)$ on $\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^2$, where $\widehat{R_1 f}(\xi)=-i\frac{\xi_1}{|\xi|}\hat f(\xi)$. Decide whether every $u_0\in H^1(\mathbb R^2)$ gives a global solution in $C(\mathbb R,H^1)$.

title: KdV with a cosine coefficient
plain: Put a cos x in front of the cubic term of modified KdV on the circle. Energy survives but the L² norm no longer does. Can solutions blow up?
math: Consider $u_t+u_{xxx}+(\cos(x)\,u^3)_x=0$ on $\mathbb T=\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z$, which conserves $\int u$ and $\int(\tfrac12u_x^2-\tfrac14\cos(x)u^4)$ but not $\int u^2$. Decide whether every $u_0\in C^\infty(\mathbb T)$ yields a global smooth solution.

title: Quintic Szegő growth
plain: The cubic Szegő equation on the circle is integrable and its solutions' high Sobolev norms can grow without bound. Decide what the quintic version does.
math: For $iu_t=\Pi(|u|^4u)$ on $L^2_+(\mathbb T)$ ($\Pi$ the Szegő projector), decide whether there is $u_0\in C^\infty\cap L^2_+$ with $\limsup_{t\to\infty}\|u(t)\|_{H^s}=\infty$ for some $s>\tfrac12$.

title: L⁴ Strichartz on a cube
plain: On a flat square torus the L⁴ Strichartz estimate holds with only ε loss of derivatives. Prove the same on the surface of a cube, where corners diffract waves.
math: Let $S$ be the flat unit-cube surface. Prove that for every $\varepsilon>0$, $\|e^{it\Delta}f\|_{L^4([0,1]\times S)}\le C_\varepsilon\|f\|_{H^\varepsilon(S)}$.

title: Scattering on the cube corner
plain: Defocusing cubic Schrödinger in the plane scatters for all finite-mass data. Show the same on the surface of an infinite cube corner.
math: Let $\mathcal C$ be the flat cone of angle $3\pi/2$ (boundary of an octant). Prove that every $u_0\in L^2(\mathcal C)$ gives a global solution of $iu_t+\Delta u=|u|^2u$ that scatters in $L^2$ as $t\to\pm\infty$.

title: Paley spin glass
plain: Spins on F_p interact through Legendre symbols of their differences. The spectral bound caps the ground-state energy at one half times p^{3/2}, and local search gets to about 0.46. Is the bound sharp?
math: For primes $p\equiv1\pmod4$ let $E_p=\max_{\sigma\in\{\pm1\}^{\mathbb F_p}}\sum_{i<j}\left(\frac{j-i}{p}\right)\sigma_i\sigma_j\le\frac12p^{3/2}$. Decide whether $E_p/p^{3/2}\to\frac12$. (Greedy local search from 30 random starts gave ratios $0.461,0.461,0.461,0.456$ for $p=101,197,401,797$.)

title: Two vortices on a cube
plain: Two identical point vortices on the surface of a cube have no symmetry to make them integrable. Show their motion is chaotic.
math: Let $G$ be the Green function of the flat unit-cube surface $S$ and $R$ its Robin function. Show the Hamiltonian $H(z_1,z_2)=G(z_1,z_2)+\tfrac12(R(z_1)+R(z_2))$ on $S\times S\setminus\Delta$, with symplectic form $dA_1+dA_2$, has an energy level on which the flow has positive topological entropy.

title: Chaos in the double pendulum at every energy
plain: The planar double pendulum with equal masses and arms is chaotic at moderate energies. Prove it is chaotic at every energy above the rest state, however small.
math: Let $H$ be the Hamiltonian of the planar double pendulum with $m_1=m_2=\ell_1=\ell_2=g=1$, with minimum $E_0$. Prove that for every $E>E_0$ the flow on $\{H=E\}$ has positive topological entropy.

title: Ising spin at a cube corner
plain: Glue three quarter-planes of the square grid into the surface of an infinite cube corner and run the critical Ising model. Prove the corner spin decorrelates with the exponent 7/24 that conformal field theory predicts.
math: Let $\Gamma$ be the union of the three quadrant grids $\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^2$ on the faces of the octant boundary, glued along the axes, with apex $o$. For the critical nearest-neighbour Ising model on $\Gamma$ prove $\langle\sigma_o\sigma_x\rangle\asymp|x|^{-7/24}$ as $|x|\to\infty$.

title: Two-frequency localization
plain: Use a potential that is the sum of two cosines with frequencies √2 and √3, and take strong coupling. Prove electrons localize for these specific frequencies, not just for almost every frequency pair.
math: Let $(H_\theta\psi)(n)=\psi(n+1)+\psi(n-1)+10\big(\cos2\pi(n\sqrt2+\theta_1)+\cos2\pi(n\sqrt3+\theta_2)\big)\psi(n)$. Prove that for Lebesgue-a.e. $\theta\in\mathbb T^2$, $H_\theta$ has pure point spectrum with exponentially decaying eigenfunctions.

title: Kagome Hofstadter butterfly
plain: The Harper model on the square lattice has a Cantor spectrum for every irrational flux. Prove the same for electrons hopping on the kagome lattice.
math: Let $H_\alpha$ be the nearest-neighbour magnetic Laplacian on the kagome lattice for a uniform magnetic field with flux $2\pi\alpha$ through each unit cell. Prove that $\sigma(H_\alpha)$ is a Cantor set for every irrational $\alpha$.

title: Jacobi matrix of primes
plain: Use the primes as the off-diagonal entries of a Jacobi matrix. Known criteria for absolutely continuous spectrum just fail because prime gaps fluctuate. Decide the spectral type.
math: Let $J$ be the Jacobi matrix on $\ell^2(\mathbb N)$ with $a_n=p_n$ (the $n$-th prime) and $b_n=0$, which is self-adjoint since $\sum1/p_n=\infty$. Decide whether the spectrum of $J$ is purely absolutely continuous on $\mathbb R$.

title: Fibonacci-modulated growing Jacobi matrix
plain: Off-diagonal weights grow like √n but are doubled wherever the Fibonacci word has a 1. Periodic modulations give spectral phase transitions. Decide what this aperiodic one gives.
math: Let $f\in\{0,1\}^{\mathbb N}$ be the Fibonacci word and $J$ the Jacobi matrix with $a_n=\sqrt n\,(1+f_n)$, $b_n=0$. Determine the spectral type of $J$; in particular decide whether $J$ has absolutely continuous spectrum.

title: Hearing tetrahedra
plain: Triangles can be heard: their Dirichlet spectrum determines them. Show the same holds for tetrahedra.
math: Prove that two tetrahedra in $\mathbb R^3$ with the same Dirichlet Laplacian spectrum are congruent.

title: Sofa for every angle
plain: Find the optimal sofa for a hallway turning by any angle, not just 90°.
math: For every $\theta\in(0,\pi)$, determine the optimal sofa for the width-1 corridor turning by $\theta$.

title: Hat Ising universality
plain: Magnets on a hat tiling should behave at their critical point exactly like magnets on a square grid.
math: Prove the hat-graph Ising model has critical exponents $\beta=1/8$, $\gamma=7/4$, $\nu=1$.

title: Finite simple groups in Lean
plain: Turn the classification of finite simple groups into one computer-checked proof.
math: Formalize the classification of finite simple groups in Lean 4.

title: Alternating prime residues
plain: Find ten consecutive primes whose remainders mod 4 alternate 1, 3, 1, 3, …, and infinitely many such runs.
math: Prove infinitely many $n$ with $p_{n+i}\equiv 2+(-1)^{i}\pmod 4$ for $0\le i<10$.

title: Counting Prime Nim losses
plain: Show the losing positions of Prime Nim thin out at a precise power rate.
math: Prove $|L\cap[1,x]|=x^{\alpha+o(1)}$ for some $\alpha$ and compute it.

title: Primes a² + b⁴ with prime inputs
plain: Show infinitely many primes are a square of a prime plus a fourth power of a prime.
math: Prove infinitely many primes of the form $p^2+q^4$ with $p,q$ prime.

title: Doubly smooth neighbours
plain: Find infinitely many primes whose two neighbours have only small prime factors.
math: Prove infinitely many primes $p$ with $P(p-1),P(p+1)\le p^{0.1}$.

title: High-dimensional sofa
plain: How does the best sofa's volume grow in an n-dimensional corridor?
math: Determine the asymptotics in $n$ of the optimal volume in the $n$-dimensional right-angled corridor of unit cross-section.

title: Polykite structure theorem
plain: Classify every shape of up to 20 kites: tiles periodically, tiles only aperiodically, or fails within a few layers.
math: Prove each polykite with $\le20$ kites either tiles periodically, tiles only aperiodically, or has Heesch number $\le10$.

title: Time-independent force
plain: Make viscous fluid blow up with a push that never changes in time.
math: Construct smooth compactly supported time-independent $f$ such that 3D Navier–Stokes from rest blows up in finite time.

title: Stable blow-up
plain: Show the 2026 Navier–Stokes blow-up still happens after any tiny change to the setup.
math: Prove the 2026 forced blow-up is stable under small smooth perturbations of $(u_0,f)$ in a suitable topology.

title: Prime-speed lonely runners
plain: Prove the lonely runner conjecture when every speed is a prime number.
math: For distinct primes $p_1,\dots,p_n$, prove $\sup_t\min_i\|tp_i\|\ge\frac1{n+1}$.

title: Counting minimal Sudokus
plain: How many uniquely solvable Sudokus with no removable clue exist, as the board grows?
math: Find the asymptotics of the number of minimal uniquely solvable $n^2\times n^2$ puzzles.

title: Fluid in a box blows up
plain: Show viscous fluid in a closed box with sticky walls can blow up under a smooth push.
math: Construct smooth $f$ such that 3D Navier–Stokes with no-slip in the unit cube blows up in finite time.

title: Divisor-balanced primes
plain: Show infinitely many primes p have p − 1 and p + 1 with the same number of divisors.
math: Prove infinitely many primes $p$ with $d(p-1)=d(p+1)$.

title: Homogenized wildfire
plain: Fire spreads through random patches of two fuel types. Show it has a definite average speed and compute it.
math: For the eikonal equation with i.i.d. two-valued speed on a lattice, prove homogenization and give the effective speed in closed form.

title: Galois groups of Keller fibers
plain: Find the symmetry group of the preimages of a point under the 2026 Keller maps.
math: Compute the Galois group of the generic fiber of Gallagher's degree-$n$ Keller family for each $n\ge3$.

title: Convex sofa
plain: Find the best convex sofa.
math: Maximize area over convex sets admissible in the width-1 right-angled corridor.

title: Squares on a sphere
plain: Every closed curve on a sphere should pass through the corners of a spherical square.
math: Prove every Jordan curve on $S^2$ inscribes a spherical quadrilateral with equal sides and equal angles.

title: Cross-polytopes in 4D
plain: Every 4D convex body should have the corners of a regular cross-polytope on its boundary.
math: Prove every convex body in $\mathbb{R}^4$ has an inscribed regular cross-polytope.

title: Prime-graceful forests
plain: Label any forest so the edge differences are exactly the first m primes.
math: Prove every forest with $m$ edges has an injective $\ell:V\to\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$ whose edge differences are $\{p_1,\dots,p_m\}$.

title: Doubled-twin sieve upper bound
plain: Bound the number of doubled-twin quadruples up to x by the predicted count times at most 3.
math: Prove $\#\{p\le x: p,p+2,2p+1,2p+3\text{ prime}\}\le(3+o(1))\,\mathfrak{S}x/\log^4x$, with $\mathfrak S$ the singular series.

title: Hyperoperation fixed points
plain: In any natural real-rank hyperoperation family, show the rank at which 2 ∘ 2 stops being 4 is not a whole number.
math: For the unique analytic family $a[s]b$ satisfying the recursion and log-convexity in $s$, prove $\{s: 2[s]2=4\}$ is exactly $[1,\infty)\cap$ an explicit closed set and determine whether it is an interval.

title: Graceful forests with one big tree
plain: A forest with c trees and m edges is graceful-forest labelled if its vertices get the labels 0 to m + c − 1 with all edge differences distinct. Show this works whenever there are at least two trees and one of them holds more than half the edges.
math: Prove every forest with $m$ edges and $c\ge2$ components, one of which has more than $m/2$ edges, has a bijection $V\to\{0,\dots,m+c-1\}$ with all $|\ell(u)-\ell(v)|$, $uv\in E$, distinct.

title: Keller maps with integer fibers
plain: Show no Jacobian-conjecture counterexample with integer coefficients is injective on integer points but not invertible.
math: Prove every Keller map $F\in\mathbb{Z}[x,y,z]^3$ injective on $\mathbb{Z}^3$ is a polynomial automorphism of $\mathbb{C}^3$.

title: Tetris on a cylinder
plain: When the board wraps left to right, can a player survive forever against any piece sequence?
math: Decide whether a player can survive indefinitely in a width-10 cylindrical Tetris well against adversarial piece sequences with 1-piece preview.

title: Prime-sum labelling of balanced trees
plain: Label a tree with 1 to n so every edge sums to a prime. Parity forces the two sides of the tree to be balanced. Show balance is enough, for large n.
math: Prove every tree on $n\ge n_0$ vertices whose bipartition classes have sizes $\lceil n/2\rceil,\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ admits a bijection $V\to[n]$ with all edge sums prime.

title: Hyperdissipative forced blow-up
plain: Fluids with extra strong viscosity never blow up above a known threshold. Show forced blow-up still happens just below it.
math: For $\partial_tu+(u\cdot\nabla)u+\nabla p=-(-\Delta)^{\alpha}u+f$ on $\mathbb{R}^3$, construct smooth compactly supported $f$ giving finite-time blow-up from rest for every $\alpha<5/4$.

title: Hat Ising critical line
plain: Ising models on a hat tiling and its dual should be exactly related at their critical points. Prove the duality relation holds rigorously.
math: For the ferromagnetic Ising model on the hat graph $G$ and its planar dual $G^*$, prove $\sinh(2\beta_c(G))\sinh(2\beta_c(G^*))=1$.

title: Blow-up near a wall
plain: Show the 2026 forced blow-up mechanism also works in a half-space with no-slip wall, with the singularity on the wall.
math: Construct smooth compactly supported $f$ such that Navier–Stokes in $\mathbb{R}^3_+$ with no-slip, from rest, blows up in finite time at a boundary point.

title: Unit distances in three dimensions after 2026
plain: The 2026 number-field idea beat Erdős in the plane. Adapt it to unit distances among points on a sphere in 3D.
math: Prove there are $n$-point sets on the unit sphere $S^2$ with $\ge n^{1+c}$ pairs at distance $1$, for some $c>0$ and infinitely many $n$.

title: Lonely runner gap for the first n primes
plain: For the first n primes as speeds, find the actual loneliness gap asymptotically.
math: Determine the asymptotics of $\delta_n=\sup_t\min_{i\le n}\|tp_i\|$ as $n\to\infty$.

title: Hat dominoes freeze
plain: Random domino-style pairings of hat tiles inside a large region with a fixed boundary develop a frozen outer zone. Find the shape of the boundary between frozen and random regions.
math: For uniform perfect matchings of the hat graph on regions $L\cdot\Omega$, prove an arctic curve exists and identify it for $\Omega$ a regular hexagon.

title: Square Nim from both ends
plain: Two piles; a move removes a square from one pile or the same square from both. Find the losing positions' asymptotic density.
math: For moves $(a,b)\to(a-k^2,b),(a,b-k^2),(a-k^2,b-k^2)$, prove $\#\{(a,b)\in[N]^2:\mathcal P\}=N^{1+\theta+o(1)}$ and find $\theta$.

title: Monochromatic square-sum triangles, many colours
plain: Colour the positive integers with any finite number of colours. Show there are always three numbers of one colour whose pairwise sums are all squares.
math: Prove that for every $r$ and every $r$-colouring of $\mathbb{N}$ there are distinct $a,b,c$ of one colour with $a+b,a+c,b+c$ all perfect squares.

title: Keller monodromy is everything
plain: Show every symmetric group appears as the hidden symmetry group of the fibres of some 3D Jacobian-conjecture counterexample.
math: Prove that for each $n\ge3$ there is a non-invertible Keller map $\mathbb{C}^3\to\mathbb{C}^3$ of geometric degree $n$ whose generic monodromy group is $S_n$.

title: Seven-free squares
plain: Count the numbers up to x whose square has no digit 7. Show the count matches the random-digit prediction.

title: Missing digits in two bases
plain: Show infinitely many primes have no digit 9 in base 10 and no digit 10 in base 11 at the same time.
math: Prove infinitely many primes whose base-10 expansion avoids the digit 9 and whose base-11 expansion avoids the digit 10.

title: Spanning trees inside the prime-sum graph
plain: Show every balanced tree of bounded degree on 2n vertices can be laid out on 1 to 2n so all its edges sum to primes.
math: Prove that for every $\Delta$ there is $n_0$ such that every tree on $2n\ge n_0$ vertices with maximum degree $\le\Delta$ and bipartition classes of size $n$ is a spanning subgraph of the prime-sum graph on $[2n]$.

title: Spanning trees inside the square-sum graph
plain: Show every tree of maximum degree 3 on N vertices fits inside the square-sum graph on 1 to N.
math: Prove every tree on $N\ge N_0$ vertices with maximum degree $\le3$ is a spanning subgraph of $S_N$.

title: AKLT on the hat
plain: Show the AKLT quantum spin model placed on a hat tiling has an energy gap above its ground state.
math: For the AKLT Hamiltonian on the vertex graph of a hat tiling (spin $d(v)/2$ at vertex $v$), prove a uniform spectral gap on finite patches.

title: Quasi-independence of square-plus-one steps
plain: Show the largest prime factors of n² + 1 and (n + 1)² + 1 are nearly independent in size.

title: Prime Nim's mod-3 bias
plain: Losing pile sizes in Prime Nim are about three times as likely to be 1 mod 3 as 0 mod 3. Find the exact limiting proportions.
math: For the prime subtraction game, prove the limits $\lim_x\#\{n\le x:G(n)=0,\ n\equiv r\ (3)\}/\#\{n\le x:G(n)=0\}$ exist for $r=0,1,2$, and determine them.

title: Bombieri–Vinogradov for seven-free primes in base 10
plain: Show seven-free primes are well distributed in arithmetic progressions on average over moduli up to x^θ, for some θ > 0, in base 10.
math: Prove there is $\theta>0$ such that $\sum_{q\le x^\theta}\max_{(a,q)=1}\big|\pi_7(x;q,a)-\frac{\pi_7(x)}{\varphi(q)}\big|\ll_A \pi_7(x)(\log x)^{-A}$, where $\pi_7$ counts 7-free primes (moduli coprime to 10).

title: Large prime factors of 2^n + 3^n
plain: Show the largest prime factor of 2^n + 3^n grows faster than n².
math: Prove $P(2^n+3^n)/n^2\to\infty$.

title: Infinite monochromatic square-sum paths
plain: Colour the positive integers red and blue. Show there is always an infinite increasing sequence of one colour in which every two consecutive terms sum to a perfect square.
math: Prove every 2-colouring of $\mathbb{N}$ admits $a_1<a_2<\cdots$ of one colour with $a_i+a_{i+1}$ a perfect square for all $i$.

title: Is Prime Nim's losing set definable?
plain: Add the set of Prime Nim losing positions to the arithmetic of addition. Is the resulting theory decidable?
math: Decide whether the first-order theory of $(\mathbb{N},+,L)$ is decidable, where $L=\{n:G(n)=0\}$ for the prime subtraction game.

title: Prime-digit continued fractions in arithmetic progressions
plain: Show there are infinitely many quadratic irrationals all of whose continued fraction digits are prime, in each real quadratic field.
math: Prove for every real quadratic field $K$ there are infinitely many $\alpha\in K$ with purely periodic continued fraction expansion having all partial quotients prime.

title: Largest prime factor of 2^n + n
plain: Show the largest prime factor of 2^n + n tends to infinity faster than any fixed multiple of n.
math: Prove $P(2^n+n)/n\to\infty$.

title: Largest prime factor of n^n + 1
plain: Show P(n^n + 1) / n tends to infinity.
math: Prove $P(n^n+1)/n\to\infty$.

title: Primes on circles centred at the origin
plain: Find the largest number of prime points (p, q) lying on a single circle centred at the origin with radius up to R.
math: Determine the order of $\max_{n\le R^2}\#\{(p,q)\in\mathbb{P}^2:p^2+q^2=n\}$.

title: Largest prime factor of Markov numbers
plain: Show the largest prime factor of Markov numbers tends to infinity.
math: Prove $P(m)\to\infty$ as $m$ runs through Markov numbers.

title: Largest factor of p² + p + 1 small
plain: Show infinitely many primes p have P(p² + p + 1) < p.
math: Prove $\#\{p\le x:P(p^2+p+1)<p\}\gg\pi(x)$.

title: Consecutive largest factors both 3 mod 4
plain: Show P(n) and P(n+1) are both 3 mod 4 for a quarter of all n.
math: Prove $\#\{n\le x:P(n)\equiv P(n+1)\equiv3\ (4)\}\sim x/4$.

title: Euler with reversed stretching
plain: Flip the sign of the vortex-stretching term in the 3D Euler equations, keeping the usual Biot–Savart law. Do smooth solutions stay smooth forever?
math:

title: Spikes at the squares
plain: Put a fixed bump at every perfect square on the half-line lattice. The spectrum has no absolutely continuous part. Prove the states are localized inside the free band.
math: Let $H=\Delta+\lambda\mathbf 1_{\{m^2:m\ge1\}}$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb N)$, $\lambda\ne0$. Prove that the spectral measure of $\delta_1$ restricted to $(-2,2)$ is pure point.

title: Non-arithmetic tones of the cube
plain: Many vibration frequencies of a cube's surface come from the square torus and are rational multiples of π². Show some frequency is not.
math: Let $S$ be the flat unit-cube surface. Prove that some eigenvalue of the Laplacian on $S$ is not a rational multiple of $\pi^2$.

title: Multiplicities on the Fermat quartic
plain: The surface x⁴+y⁴+z⁴ = 1 has the symmetries of a cube. Show its Laplace eigenvalues never repeat more than symmetry forces, except perhaps finitely often.
math: Let $S=\{x^4+y^4+z^4=1\}$ with the induced metric. Prove that all but finitely many Laplace eigenvalues of $S$ have multiplicity at most $3$.

title: Infinite knots in the ABC flow
plain: Steady Euler flows can carry knotted streamlines. Show the symmetric ABC flow has closed streamlines tied in infinitely many different knots.
math: Prove that the flow of $\dot x=\sin z+\cos y,\ \dot y=\sin x+\cos z,\ \dot z=\sin y+\cos x$ on $\mathbb T^3$ has null-homotopic periodic orbits lying in embedded balls and realizing infinitely many distinct knot types.

title: Gerver constant is transcendental
plain: Show the area of Gerver's sofa is not a root of any polynomial with integer coefficients.
math: Prove $\mu_G\approx2.2195$ is transcendental.

title: Real-rank hyperoperation uniqueness
plain: Prove there is exactly one natural way to fill in the operations between addition, multiplication and powers.
math: Prove uniqueness of an analytic family $a[s]b$ on $s\in[1,3]$ under the recursion law plus a log-convexity condition in $s$, and existence.

title: Hat ground state
plain: Find the arrangement of hat tiles that minimises a natural energy, and show it is the aperiodic tiling.
math: Prove the hat tiling is the unique (up to isometry) ground state of a finite-range two-body potential on hat-shaped particles in the plane.

title: Delayed fire on the grid
plain: If the fire only spreads every other turn, find the smallest per-turn budget that always contains it.
math: Find the infimum of average firefighter budgets that contain the half-speed fire on $\mathbb{Z}^2$.

title: Spectral gap of the spectre
plain: Find the exact gaps in the energy levels of an electron moving on a spectre tiling.
math: Prove the spectrum of the adjacency operator on the spectre tiling has gaps labelled by an explicit $K$-theory group, with every label open.

title: Three of four
plain: Show infinitely often at least three of the four doubled-twin numbers are prime at once.
math: Prove there are infinitely many $n$ such that at least three of $n,n+2,2n+1,2n+3$ are prime.

title: Hyperbolic Hex
plain: On a board tiled by heptagons in hyperbolic space, find an explicit first-player win for Hex-like connection.
math: On the $(7,3)$ tiling with a disk of radius $r$ split into four boundary arcs, give an explicit winning strategy for the first player for all $r$.

title: Few loops for square-plus-one
plain: The square-plus-one map has a loop: 89 goes to 233 and back. Show there are only finitely many loops.
math: Prove $Q(n)=P(n^2+1)$ has finitely many periodic orbits (one is $89\leftrightarrow233$).

title: Strict convexity of hat first-passage
plain: Give each hat-tile edge an independent random length. Prove the limiting ball of first-passage distances is strictly convex.
math: For i.i.d. continuous edge weights with finite exponential moment on the hat adjacency graph, prove the first-passage limit shape exists and is strictly convex.

title: Sandpile identity on hats
plain: The abelian sandpile on a large hat-tiled region has an identity element that looks like a fractal picture. Show it has a scaling limit.
math: Prove the sandpile identity on hat-tiled $L$-balls, rescaled by $L$, converges weakly (as a height-density measure) and that the limit is not rotationally invariant.

title: Affine prime maps all settle
plain: Fix whole numbers a and b. Send a prime p to the largest prime factor of ap + b. Every case tested falls into a loop. Prove this always happens.
math: Prove that for all fixed integers $a\ge2$, $b\ge1$, every orbit of $p\mapsto P(ap+b)$ on primes is eventually periodic.

title: Longest increasing run of prime gaps
plain: Among the first N prime gaps, find the longest subsequence that strictly increases. Show it grows like a power of N and find the power.
math: Let $L(N)$ be the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence of $(p_{n+1}-p_n)_{n\le N}$. Prove $L(N)=N^{\theta+o(1)}$ and determine $\theta$.

title: Undecidable prime-factor maps
plain: Show no algorithm can decide, given a and b, whether every orbit of n ↦ n/2 (even) or the largest prime factor of an + b (odd) eventually loops.
math: Prove $\{(a,b)\in\mathbb{N}^2:$ every orbit of $n\mapsto n/2$ ($n$ even), $P(an+b)$ ($n$ odd) is eventually periodic$\}$ is not recursive, or prove it is.

title: Digit-restricted Chowla
plain: Show μ(n)μ(n+1) has no bias on numbers n where neither n nor n+1 contains the digit 7.
math: Prove $\sum_{n\le x,\ 7\notin n,\ 7\notin n+1}\mu(n)\mu(n+1)=o(x^{\log9/\log10})$.

title: Minimal degree of a Jacobian counterexample
plain: The 2026 counterexamples have degree 7. Find the smallest degree any 3D counterexample can have.
math: Determine $\min\{\deg F: F:\mathbb{C}^3\to\mathbb{C}^3$ non-invertible Keller map$\}$.

title: Square-plus-one orbits rarely loop
plain: Show almost every starting number's square-plus-one sequence never repeats.
math: Prove the set of $n$ whose orbit under $Q(n)=P(n^2+1)$ is eventually periodic has natural density 0.

title: Exponential growth of square-plus-one orbits
plain: Show square-plus-one sequences, when they don't loop, grow at a steady exponential rate in the number of digits.
math: Prove that for almost every $n$ (density 1), $\lim_{k}\frac1k\log\log Q^k(n)$ exists and equals a constant $\gamma>0$; identify $\gamma$.

title: Hat percolation is conformally invariant
plain: Show critical percolation on the hat tiling's tiles has crossing probabilities given by Cardy's formula.
math: For critical site percolation on hat tiles, prove crossing probabilities of conformal rectangles converge to Cardy's formula as the mesh $\to0$.

title: Critical Ising on the hat is SLE(3)
plain: Show the interface in the critical Ising model on a hat tiling converges to the random curve SLE(3), even though the graph is not isoradial.
math: For the critical Ising model on the hat graph with Dobrushin boundary conditions, prove the interface converges to chordal SLE$_3$.

title: Square-sum Ramsey with many colours
plain: Colour 1 to N with r colours. Show some colour contains four numbers whose six pairwise sums are all squares, once N is large enough.
math: Prove that for every $r$ there is $N$ such that every $r$-colouring of $[N]$ has a monochromatic $K_4$ in $S_N$, or show it fails for some $r$.

title: Undecidability of Prime Nim variants
plain: Show there is no algorithm that takes a polynomial f and decides whether the subtraction game with moves {f(p) : p prime} has eventually periodic Grundy values.
math: Prove $\{f\in\mathbb{Z}[x]:\text{Grundy sequence of the game with move set }f(\mathbb{P})\cap\mathbb{N}\text{ is eventually periodic}\}$ is undecidable, or decidable.

title: Chaotic billiards in a superellipse
plain: The billiard table x⁴+y⁴ ≤ 1 is smooth and convex but has four flat points, so it has no caustics. Show a positive fraction of its phase space is chaotic.
math: Let $\Phi$ be the billiard map of $\{x^4+y^4\le1\}$ with its invariant Liouville measure $\nu$. Prove that the metric entropy $h_\nu(\Phi)$ is positive.

title: Ergodicity of the regular tetrahedron billiard
plain: The regular tetrahedron does not tile space, so its billiard cannot be unfolded into a straight-line flow on a torus. Is a billiard ball in it ergodic?
math: Prove or disprove that the billiard flow in a regular tetrahedron in $\mathbb R^3$ is ergodic with respect to Liouville measure on the unit tangent bundle.

title: Quartic oscillator ground state
plain: The lowest energy of the quartic oscillator, −d²/dx² + x⁴, is about 1.0603620905. Show it is irrational.
math: Let $E_0=\min\sigma\big(-\frac{d^2}{dx^2}+x^4\big)$ on $L^2(\mathbb R)$. Prove $E_0\notin\mathbb Q$.

title: Square-sum chromatic number
plain: Find exactly how many colors the infinite square-sum graph needs.
math: Determine $\chi(S_\infty)$ exactly.

title: Cube-sum independence
plain: Find the largest set of numbers up to N where no two add to a cube.
math: Determine $\alpha(C_N)$ asymptotically, with second-order term.

title: Keller maps classification
plain: List every Jacobian-conjecture counterexample in 3D, up to symmetry.
math: Classify all non-invertible Keller maps $\mathbb{C}^3\to\mathbb{C}^3$ up to composition with polynomial automorphisms.

title: Firefighter on Z³
plain: How many firefighters per turn are needed to contain a fire in 3D, as a precise growth rate?
math: Determine $\lim_{t\to\infty}f(t)/t$ for the minimal firefighters needed to contain fire on $\mathbb{Z}^3$ by time $t$.

title: Sudoku count asymptotics
plain: Count n²×n² Sudoku grids exactly, to leading order.
math: Prove $\#\text{Sudoku}(n)=\left(\frac{(n^2)!^{2}}{n^{2n^2}e^{\dots}}\right)\!(1+o(1))$ with an explicit leading term.

title: Polykite complete classification
plain: For every polykite, decide whether it tiles, and if so how.
math: Give an algorithm deciding, for any single polykite, whether it tiles the plane, and prove it correct.

title: Origami with a bounded number of layers
plain: Find the best origami base for any tree when no point may have more than 4 layers of paper.
math: Give an algorithm for the minimal square paper for uniaxial bases of metric trees with layer count at most 4, with proof of optimality.

title: Square-plus-one merging
plain: Many square-plus-one sequences run into the one starting at 2. Decide whether every sequence eventually does, apart from those caught in loops.
math: Decide whether every $n\ge2$ whose $Q$-orbit is not eventually periodic satisfies $Q^a(n)=Q^b(2)$ for some $a,b$.

title: Unforced blow-up near the forced one
plain: Show the known forced Navier–Stokes blow-up can be made to work with forcing that decays to zero at the blow-up time.
math: Prove there exist smooth $u_0$ and $f\in L^1_tL^2_x\cap C^\infty$ with $\|f(t)\|_{L^2}\to0$ as $t\to T^-$ such that the forced 3D NS solution blows up at $T$.

title: Spikes at the primes
plain: Put a fixed bump at every prime on the half-line lattice. Prove the electron is localized at energies inside the free band, as it would be if the primes were random.
math: Let $H=\Delta+\lambda\mathbf 1_{\mathbb P}$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb N)$, $\lambda\ne0$. Prove that $H$ has pure point spectrum in $(-2,2)$.

title: Optimal 3D origami
plain: For every 3D shape, find the smallest sheet of paper that folds into it.
math: Give a characterization, with an algorithm, of the minimal-area square that folds into any given polyhedral surface.
